title: Why Traffic Congestion Grows Exponentially, Why It Matters, and What To Do About It // An Explainer
summary: CityNerd explains why traffic congestion grows nonlinearly as more cars use a road network, and why adding road capacity tends not to fix it. It covers the consequences for drivers, bus riders, cyclists and pedestrians, and discusses alternatives such as true bus rapid transit.
why: HN commenters cite it when arguing that congestion is an exponential, feedback-driven problem so widening roads or removing a few cars behaves counterintuitively.

quote.text: traffic congestion is an exponential problem
